verdict_reason: Every emitted statistic reproduces an independent recomputation exactly. Fertility is the micro-average total_tokens / total whitespace-delimited words, which is Ali et al. section 3.4's definition (NOT a mean of per-document ratios), and on four real tokenizers over the shipped corpus BLME and my own Counter-based recomputation agree to 0.0 absolute: gpt2 1.184466019417476 (244/206), pythia-70m 1.203883495145631 (248/206), distilgpt2 1.184466019417476, bert-base-uncased 1.140776699029126 (235/206). Shannon token entropy matches scipy.stats.entropy on the same counts to 0.0 (1.8e-15 on one model, pure summation order). The one design choice worth re-deriving is `len(tokenizer)` rather than `tokenizer.vocab_size` for V, and it is right: ids actually produced can exceed the base vocabulary, which would push both emitted fractions outside [0,1].
comparable_reason: Fertility itself IS comparable across models on a locked corpus and word convention -- that is the entire point of the metric -- but the bundle as a whole is not a structural measurement. `vocab_size` is a config constant read straight off the tokenizer. `_meta_vocab_utilization` is (distinct ids seen)/V on a FIXED corpus, so its numerator is near-constant across models and the column is essentially 1/V. And `_meta_normalised_token_entropy` is not an entropy normaliser at all: holding the tokenizer AND the true distribution fixed (two symbols, exactly 50/50, H = ln 2 at every size) and changing only the number of observations, it reads 1.000000 / 0.500000 / 0.301030 / 0.231378 / 0.150515 / 0.130824 at T = 2/4/10/20/100/200. It is a readout of log(T). All ten keys are correctly rejected by the downstream predictor gate.
github_reason: I verified the ESTIMAND rather than re-running the released loader this round: BLME's fertility is total pieces over total words, which is what Rust et al.'s analyze_UD_file accumulates and what Ali et al. section 3.4 defines, and I reproduced BLME's value bit-for-bit from an independent Counter over the same tokenizer calls on four tokenizer families. The one substantive divergence from Rust et al. is deliberate and is a WORD CONVENTION, not an arithmetic one: they segment with UD tokenisation (punctuation is its own word) and BLME uses Ali's whitespace split, so on 'The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.' the two give 10/10 = 1.0 and 10/9 = 1.111... respectively. task_metadata.py:71 leaves the repository field empty and should name adapter-hub/hgiyt.
paper_reason: Rust et al. Figure 1b is computed on UD v2.6 train/dev with their cased English tokenizer, and Ali et al. section 3.4 on 10000 held-out documents; neither corpus is available locally, and both quantities are corpus-defined, so there is no protocol-free published scalar to hit. On BLME's own shipped 20-sentence corpus gpt2 fertility is 1.184466019417476 -- a well-defined number, but not a reproduction of anyone's figure.
confounds_reason: By construction, and the file says so honestly. The corpus is fixed, so total_words = 206 and total_chars are constants across models and fertility, _meta_compression_ratio and _meta_total_tokens are the SAME degree of freedom rescaled (Pearson 1.0) -- which is why the latter two are correctly demoted. vocab_size is an architecture constant; _meta_vocab_utilization is its reciprocal. Holding text and tokenizer fixed and changing the model argument changes every output by exactly 0.0, confirming this is a tokenizer diagnostic and not a representation measurement. That makes the whole bundle a control variable, and the pipeline treats it as one.
defects: CODE / ZERO-WORD FERTILITY IS FABRICATED (tokenizer_efficiency.py:128, `total_tokens / max(1, total_words)`). On the input '   ' the real gpt2 tokenizer emits 3 tokens and the text has 0 whitespace words, and the task reports fertility = 3.0 with _meta_total_words = 0 -- a tokens-per-word ratio with no words. The guard should mark the ratio undefined (NaN) rather than silently substituting a denominator of 1. Reachable on any whitespace-only or punctuation-only document.

NORMALIZATION / _meta_normalised_token_entropy IS A SAMPLE-SIZE READOUT. Dividing by log(min(T, V)) was introduced to stop it being a vocabulary readout, and it succeeds at that -- but at fixed true entropy it now falls as 1/log(T): 1.000000 -> 0.130824 from T = 2 to T = 200 with H pinned at exactly ln 2. It is _meta_-gated, and the entropy ceiling is emitted as _meta_entropy_ceiling_n, so this is disclosed rather than hidden; it must not be read as a normalised entropy.

CODE / ITERATION ORDER (tokenizer_efficiency.py:96-103): `list(dataset)` materialises the whole iterable before `dataset[:num_samples]` is applied, so a 10000-row generator is fully consumed to tokenize 20 rows. Resource handling only; the finite result is unaffected.

CODE / UNVALIDATED CONTRACT (:166-168): vocab_utilization and normalised_token_entropy are clipped into [0,1] rather than validated. If a tokenizer reports V smaller than the number of distinct ids it emits, the clip hides the inconsistency instead of surfacing it. On all four real tokenizers I checked this never fires.

PROTOCOL / WORD CONVENTION: fertility uses Ali's whitespace split, not Rust's UD segmentation, and the two differ by roughly the punctuation rate (1.111 vs 1.000 on the module's own first sentence). Both are legitimate; the docstring cites both papers without saying which convention is implemented.

DOCUMENTATION: docs/TOP_PREDICTORS.md section 2 still lists four tokenizer predictors at +0.71 to +0.77 partial rho, of which three are the same number rescaled by corpus constants and all four are now rejected by the predictor gate. The module docstring already flags this; the table has not been updated.
